title: PR1- French test next week
body:
Dear Parents,
I would like to inform you that the children will have their first French test next week. The aim is to review what we have been learning in class and give the children an opportunity to show what they can understand and say in French.
The test will include two parts:
1. Listening (Écouter)
The listening activities will always include pictures to help the children understand what they hear. The children will need to listen carefully and match what they hear to the correct pictures. Depending on the exercise, they may need to circle the correct number or write the corresponding number next to the correct picture.
The listening part will cover:
Understanding greetings (Salut, Bonjour, Au revoir)
Recognising numbers from 0 to 12.
Recognising some colours and geometric shapes and matching them to the correct pictures by numbering them.
2. Speaking (Parler)
The children will be asked to:
Say their name and age in French.
Say the numbers from 0 to 12.
Name colours and geometric shapes in French.
Some students did not have their plastic folder with them today. The folder should be at home and contains all the French vocabulary we have been learning in class. Please help your child revise the vocabulary in the folder, especially greetings, numbers from 0 to 12, colours, geometric shapes, and how to introduce themselves in French. As this is their first French test, the aim is also to help the children become familiar with this type of assessment and build their confidence. Please encourage them to practise in a relaxed and playful way.
Thank you very much for your support!
Kind regards,
Mme Conde

title: PR1 - Traditions Topic
body:
Dear Parents,
For our next unit of Enquiry we will be exploring different traditions and investigating the question, "How can traditions help us find out about the past?" During this unit, the children will explore what traditions are, how they pass from one generation to another, how they can change over time, and how we can use stories, photographs, and objects as evidence to learn about the past. We know that children often learn most meaningfully when they can connect new ideas to their own lives, experiences, and families. Therefore, we would like to give the children the opportunity to share traditions from their own families.
We would love to welcome a parent, grandparent, or other family member into the classroom as a "family historian" to help share one tradition from your family or culture. There is no expectation that a tradition needs to be connected to a particular country or culture. Every family has traditions, and we want to hear about the ones that matter most to your family. This could be a tradition connected to a celebration, food, music, clothing, a special day, a family activity, story, or simply something your family has done for generations. Of course, we know that families are busy, so there is absolutely no obligation to take part. We will still be exploring lots of traditions in class.
If you are interested in visiting, you would not need to prepare a formal presentation. It would be an informal, show-and-tell-style discussion. We would like the children to have the opportunity to listen, ask questions, and think like historians. If possible, it would be wonderful if you could bring one piece of evidence connected to the tradition, such as a photograph, a book/story, object, or recipe.
If you would like to participate, please send us an email telling us which date you would like to visit. The possible dates and times would be as follows:

title: PR1 - Pokemon Cards
body:
Dear Parents,
We would like to bring to your attention an agreement we have made with the Primary 1 class regarding Pokemon cards.
We believe that allowing the children to share and trade their Pokemon cards at school, with clear boundaries, can provide valuable opportunities for social and personal development. Therefore, we are keen to work with the class to create clear rules around when and how cards can be traded during the school day, without negatively impacting lesson time.
When can Pokemon cards be played with?
The children are allowed to bring their Pokemon cards to school to play with and trade during the outdoor play times in the morning and after lunch. It's important that the children are only playing with their cards at these times, and put their cards away as soon as the bell rings. Pokemon cards should not be played with in the classroom or during lesson time.
How many Pokemon cards can be brought to school?
We have noticed that some children are bringing a large quantity of cards with them to school, and as a result they spend a very long time getting ready for break, and tidying up their cards at the end of a break. This means that the transition between lesson times and break times is often very long which greatly impacts our routine and loses valuable lesson time.
Together with the class, we discussed the importance of being able to carry our Pokemon cards alone and in one hand (if we need a friend to help us carry the cards, there are simply too many), so we can also carry our snack boxes and water bottles to/from the playground safely. To help the children identify what is a "good amount" of Pokemon cards to bring to school, we have agreed that each day, the children may bring only one of the following:
1 box of Pokemon cards
1 book of Pokemon cards
1 pile of Pokemon cards
In a box or book, the children may carry as many Pokemon cards as they wish (as long as they fit in the box/book). For loose Pokemon cards, we ask that the children bring no more than 20 and that the cards are organised into one pile with an elastic band (for extra large cards, no more than 10).​
Please see the photo below for an example of what the children may bring.

This is an agreement we have made as a class, and something we expect all the children to follow from now on. We have discussed this in detail with the class, but we would greatly appreciate it if you could also remind your child of this agreement at home.
We thank you for your support with this.
Kind regards,
Gaby Rayment and Xenia Faux

**From:** Marvin Biehl <mbiehl@tandem-ims.ch>
**Date:** Fri, 06 Nov 2026 13:15:47 +0100

Liebe Eltern,

Da Piota leider nicht mehr nutzbar ist, teile ich Ihnen nun per Mail mit, dass wir nächsten Donnerstag (12. Nov 2026) einen Mathe Test haben. Ich habe den Kindern ein Übungspaket mitgegeben, das sowohl die gelben, als auch die grünen Aufgaben umfasst.

Ich habe ausserdem von einigen Eltern ein Feedback zu einer Aufgabe des grünen Aufgabenpakets bekommen, dass diese nicht lösbar sei. Das liegt daran, dass vom Lehrmittel nur Übungen zu den gelben Aufgaben verfügbar sind und die Übungen zu den erweiterten Lernzielen muss ich selbst erstellen. Ich gebe mir sehr viel Mühe sicherzustellen, dass alle selbsterstellten Aufgaben richtig sind, aber manchmal passiert mir auch ein Fehler. Ich bitte dies zu entschuldigen.

Mit freundlichen Grüssen
Biehl

title: [P3 Ale] French Test - lesson 3
body:
For listening, your child will listen to adjectives and choose the matching pictures.
For reading, your child will identify whether adjectives are in their masculine or feminine form, using what they have learned in Lesson 3.
For writing, your child will need to learn both affirmative and negative sentences to describe what to do and what not to do.
Écouter
Comprendre des adjectifs entendus et les associer à une image.
Lire
Reconnaître la forme masculine ou féminine d’un adjectif, selon les notions étudiées dans la leçon 3.
Écrire
Rédiger un itinéraire en utilisant des phrases affirmatives et négatives.
